theme: The walls that make a dinner unforgettable

linkedin.text:
Give a group a hotel ballroom and you have to manufacture atmosphere. Give them a fortified kasbah and the atmosphere is already there.

This is southern Morocco, on a trip we produced. Rammed-earth walls, a courtyard that has been hosting gatherings for centuries, and a group walking in without anyone needing to explain why it matters.

Historic venues are the best and worst thing in event production. Best, because nothing you build competes with them. Worst, because they were not designed for you: power is limited, load-in is often by hand, there is rarely a kitchen that can plate for two hundred, and the site closes to the public at a fixed hour whether or not your truck has arrived.

All of that is solvable, and all of it has to be solved before the brief is signed rather than after. That is the difference between a venue that photographs well and an evening that runs well.

Want a room with genuine weight for 2026? Send us the brief.
